content:
What we can be certain of is that Apple will raise the price of the iPhone 18 Pro when it goes on sale next month. Apple has already raised prices across its entire lineup to reflect rising memory costs, though it didn't adjust pricing on existing iPhones at the time—but that situation was always going to be temporary.

Nonetheless, two sources point to a starting price of $1,399 for this year's Pro models—but I really struggle to believe Apple would go that far…

Don't misunderstand me: Apple has made it abundantly clear to the world that it is dead serious about protecting its profit margins and isn't afraid of hefty price hikes. The MacBook Air, for example, jumped $200, from a starting price of $1,099 to $1,299. Even the MacBook Neo—which initially surprised everyone with its $599 starting price—has already been hiked by $100.

But a $300 increase on the iPhone Pro starting price is a different story. Apple has only attempted price hikes that large on its more expensive products in the past.

The biggest increase across the board came on the base-model MacBook Pro, which went from $1,699 to $1,999, a $300 jump. That kind of bump is undoubtedly massive, approaching 18%. But if the iPhone 18 Pro costs $300 more than its predecessor, the increase would balloon to a whopping 27%.

Again, this kind of increase isn't entirely impossible. Some MacBook configuration upgrades have nearly doubled in price, for instance, and Apple has always been keen on maintaining its margins. Still, Tim Cook has also hinted on earnings calls that the company isn't absolutely committed to defending margins at all costs.

On the sales side, I do think this increase would put a lot of people off upgrading, especially given that it is next year's Pro models that are really the main event.

On the other hand, the Apple Upgrade program could soften the blow of some of that increase. Consumers might feel that renting an iPhone 18 Pro for a year and then upgrading to the 20th-anniversary edition next year is a pretty good deal. But for those paying out of pocket, an increase that large is sure to give them pause.

What do you think? Do you think a $300 hike is reasonable? Or do you think even Apple wouldn't dare push a 27% increase? Share your thoughts in the comments.
